case_name: Lokesh Sharma And Anr vs The State Nct Of Delhi And Anr

parties.respondent_defendant: The State NCT of Delhi and another (wife)

facts_of_case: Petitioner husband seeks quashing of FIR registered under Sections 498A, 406, 34 IPC. Parties had arrived at a settlement whereunder wife was to receive Rs. 22,50,000/- towards full and final settlement.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the party seeking divorce to establish that the parties have arrived at a settlement.
legal_principles.held: On perusal of the aforementioned judgement and decree, it is evident that petitioner no. 1 i.e. Mr. Lokesh Sharma and respondent no. 2 i.e. Ms. Reema Sharma had taken recourse to the provisions of Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 to seek divorce, predicated on the ground of mutual consent.

legal_principles.principle: A settlement arrived at between the parties can be a valid ground for divorce.
legal_principles.held: The petition is numbered as HMA 3007/2019. By virtue of the aforesaid judgement and decree, the marriage between petitioner no. 1 i.e. Mr. Lokesh Sharma and respondent no. 2 i.e. Ms. Reema Sharma stands dissolved.

use_for_drafting: quashing FIR in domestic violence case
using Hindu Marriage Act for marriage dissolution
